Clinical Leadership
PetCure Radiation Oncology Specialists
PetCure Oncology Radiation Oncology Specialists
PetCure Oncology works with a team of talented and well-respected clinical experts to ensure your pet receives the best possible care. Each member of the PetCure Radiation Oncology Specialists group is a board-certified veterinary specialist with expertise in radiation oncology, medical oncology, or both.
Dr. Neal Mauldin, Chief Medical Officer
A pioneer in the field of veterinary radiation therapy, Dr. Mauldin has treated more than 2,000 pets with stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) since 2010
Provides clinical oversight, remote treatment planning and review, and oversees research for facilities across the PetCure Oncology network
Triple-board certified veterinarian in the fields of internal medicine, medical oncology and radiation oncology
Attained board certification in veterinary radiation oncology the first year it was offered in 1994
Has practiced as a veterinary radiation oncologist for over 30 years, including clinical leadership positions at VCA Canada Western in Calgary, Canada, the Animal Medical Center in New York City, and Louisiana State University (associate professor, section head therapeutic radiology)
Has authored over 20 peer-reviewed publications, written numerous textbook chapters, and presented invited scientific abstracts at over 40 national and international meetings pertaining to the specialty of veterinary oncology
Past president of the Veterinary Cancer Society
Training: Texas A&M University, Animal Medical Center (NYC), Memorial Sloan Kettering fellowship in radiation oncology
Pet parent to three rescued Shetland Sheepdogs (Charlotte, Jenna and Tuscan) and three horses (Briosa, Sarah and Webster)
Read Dr. Neal Mauldin’s article ‘
The New Frontiers in Veterinary Radiation Therapy
‘
Dr. Matt Arkans
Oversees radiation oncology department at PetCure Oncology at SAGE in Campbell, CA
Board-certified in veterinary radiation oncology
Prior to his current role, Dr. Arkans spent four years with MedVet as the national Specialty Leader of Radiation Oncology and clinical manager of radiation oncology at the Chicago location
Earned undergraduate degree in Biology from Franklin & Marshall College, veterinary degree from the University of Pennsylvania, and board certification from North Carolina State University
When not at work, Dr. Arkans enjoys spending time with his wife, a veterinary surgeon and his personal career hero, as well as his young son and ill-behaved lab mix, Lord Eddard Stark (AKA Eddie)
Dr. Lynda Beaver
Obtained her Doctor of Veterinary Medicine from the Ontario Veterinary College in 1989
Dedicated several years to general practice prior to transitioning to veterinary oncology
Fulfilled a four-year position as an oncology technician at the University of Wisconsin-Madison
Completed an internship in small animal medicine and surgery at the University of Illinois
Accomplished an additional oncology internship at Southern Arizona Veterinary Specialty and Emergency Center in Tucson, AZ
Completed a three-year medical oncology residency at Arizona Veterinary Specialist in 2009
Obtained board certification in medical oncology (DACVIM) in 2010
Dr. Eric Boshoven
Oversees radiation oncology, provides consults, and treats patients at PetCure Oncology at Arizona Veterinary Oncology in Phoenix, AZ, which became PetCure’s first site in May 2015
Board-certified in veterinary radiation oncology
Adjunct professor at Midwestern University in Arizona
Has been the owner of Arizona Veterinary Oncology since 2014, when he moved back to his home state and purchased the Phoenix locations of what was formerly known as Southwest Veterinary Oncology
Previously practiced for 12 years at VCA Veterinary Referral Associates in Maryland, including three years as Medical Director and six years as Intern Director
Earned veterinary degree from Colorado State University’s College of Veterinary Medicine and Biomedical Sciences before completing residency in radiation oncology at Southwest Veterinary Oncology in Tucson, AZ
A proud alumnus of the University of Arizona
Pet parent to two dogs, Captain Teague and Manny, two cats, Taz and Moo, and a macaw named Fester
Dr. Kim Cronin
Board-certified veterinary medical oncologist (Diplomate, ACVIM – Oncology)
Provides medical oncology consultations and treatment at PetCure Oncology in Clifton, NJ
Previously served as a medical oncologist at Animal Cancer Care Specialists (Acton, MA), Massachusetts Veterinary Referral Hospital (Woburn, MA), New England Veterinary Oncology Group (Waltham, MA), and Angell Memorial Animal Hospital (Boston, MA)
Founding partner of New England Veterinary Oncology Group (NEVOG), where she led the residency training program for over a decade
Former lecturer in oncology at the University of Pennsylvania School of Veterinary Medicine
Earned DVM from Cornell University College of Veterinary Medicine after completing a BS in Biology and Psychology, magna cum laude, from the College of William & Mary
Completed a small animal internship at The Animal Medical Center (NYC) and an oncology residency at North Carolina State University
Active in professional leadership, serving on multiple ACVIM committees and on the AVMA’s Council on Biologic and Therapeutic Agents (Chair 2023-2024)
Serves on the advisory council of the New England Zoo
Member of the Veterinary Cancer Society, AVMA, ACVIM, and MVMA
Dr. Tara Ehling
Dr. Ehling is board-certified in both radiation oncology and medical oncology. She is responsible for overseeing the Radiation Oncology department at PetCure Oncology Chicago in Hoffman Estates, IL beginning in early 2024.
She is a veterinary oncologist specializing in the treatment of cancer utilizing both radiation oncology and  medical oncology methods.
She aims to provide comprehensive treatment options tailored to each patient and collaborates with clients as a team to establish and achieve their care objectives.
Dr. Ehling graduated with her Doctor of Veterinary Medicine degree from Kansas State University.
She started her career in emergency medicine prior to seeking additional training in the specialty of oncology.
Dr. Ehling completed a residency in radiation oncology followed by a residency in medical oncology at Southwest Veterinary Oncology in Tucson, Arizona.
After initially entering private practice, Dr. Ehling then transitioned to the University of Missouri, College of Veterinary Medicine where she practiced as an assistant clinical professor of oncology.
When she’s not treating patients, Dr. Ehling enjoys spending time with her family and dogs. She enjoys crafts, gardening, and reading.
Dr. Molly Holmes
Provides remote telehealth visits and imaging reviews for pet owners across the country
Board-certified in veterinary radiation oncology
Joined PROS network in November 2021
Prior to joining PetCure, Dr. Holmes worked as department head and radiation oncologist in private practice in Richmond, VA and Atlanta, GA from 2019 to 2021
Dr. Holmes completed a residency in radiation oncology at Cummings School of Veterinary Medicine at Tufts University in 2017 followed by a postdoctoral fellowship at Colorado State University’s Flint Animal Cancer Center in 2018
She received her DVM degree at the University of Georgia College of Veterinary Medicine in 2014 and her Bachelor of Science in Biology at Georgia Southern University in 2010
Recently appointed as the secretary of the American College of Veterinary Radiology (ACVR), previous member of the public relations committee (ACVR) and is an active member in multiple professional organizations, including ACVR, VCS, AVMA, and the Georgia Veterinary Medical Society
Dr. Beck Mayland
Board-certified veterinary medical oncologist providing compassionate, individualized cancer care at PetCure Oncology in Clifton, NJ
Collaborates with a multidisciplinary team to design comprehensive cancer treatment plans for pets
Outside of his work at PetCure, provides remote consultations for a practice in Alaska, expanding access to care
Earned his DVM from the University of Minnesota and completed his Oncology Residency and Master’s Degree at Colorado State University
Published researcher with a focus on osteosarcoma outcomes and chemotherapy safety
Passionate educator who enjoys mentoring veterinary students and providing continuing education to colleagues
Outside of work, he enjoys exploring Colorado’s trails and spending time with his family and pets
Dr. Karri Meleo
Provides remote telehealth visits and imaging reviews for pet owners across the country
Serves as a consultant and lecturer for the Veterinary Information Network (VIN)
Board certified in both veterinary radiation and medical oncology
Attained board certification in veterinary radiation oncology the first year it was offered in 1994
Prior to joining PetCure in 2019, had worked as practicing oncologist for 30 years, most recently as Oncology Department Head for BluePearl Seattle
Earned board-certification in medical oncology (1993) following residency at The Animal Medical Center’s Donaldson-Atwood Cancer Clinic in Manhattan, NY
Earned board-certification in radiation oncology (1994) after a graduate fellowship at The Animal Medical Center’s Donaldson-Atwood Cancer Clinic and the Memorial-Sloan Kettering Cancer Center in Manhattan, NY
Has provided research support as consultant to organizations including Alpo Pet Foods, Sloan-Kettering Institute, Bayer Animal Health, Pfiser Animal Health, Meriel Limited, and more
Has authored 15 professional publications and given dozens of invited presentations on industry topics related to veterinary medical and radiation oncology
Active member of ACVR Residency Standards and Education Committee
Pet parent to Pitbull Dexter and kitties Cervantes and Ahsoka
Dr. Kelly O'Connor
Kelly O’Connor is a medical oncologist at Arizona Veterinary Oncology
Completed her undergraduate degree at the University of New Hampshire and earned her Doctor of Veterinary Medicine from Ross University School of Veterinary Medicine.
She completed a small animal rotating internship at Tufts VETS, followed by a residency in medical oncology at Cornell University.
Her passion for oncology stems from personal family cancer experiences.
Dr. O’Connor recently moved to Arizona and in her free time, she enjoys exploring local cuisine, outdoor adventures, and cheering on the Arizona Diamondbacks.
Dr. Kelsey Pohlmann
Oversees radiation oncology department, provides live remote telehealth visits, imaging reviews, and treatment planning for patients at PetCure Oncology at PVSEC in Pittsburgh and PetCure Oncology at VRIC in Clifton, NJ
Provides remote telehealth visits and imaging reviews for pet owners across the country
Board-certified in veterinary radiation oncology
Joined PROS network in October 2016
Completed residency in radiation oncology and Master’s Degree in radiation biology at Colorado State University’s prestigious Flint Animal Cancer Center
Earned both undergraduate and veterinary degrees from the University of Georgia, where she was also a three-time NCAA champion and earned eight individual All-American honors as a gymnast
Pet parent to a dog named Beamer
See Dr. Pohlmann’s interview on Milwaukee’s
The Morning Blend
Dr. Karanbir Randhawa
Dr. Karanbir Randhawa oversees the radiation oncology department at PetCure Oncology Dallas in Mansfield, TX (Opening Feb 2024).
Board-certified in veterinary radiation oncology
Dr. Randhawa attended veterinary school and completed his residency at the University of Wisconsin.
He enjoys the field of radiation oncology because it combines two subjects he finds interesting: physics and technology. “It is a field that has endless potential to improve/evolve treatment options due to improvements in technology and discovering various uses of radiation and various radiation sources.”
When he’s not helping pet patients, Dr. Randhawa enjoys spending time with his cat, Cherry Berry, and his dogs, Thorin and Balin. During his spare time, you can find him playing basketball, boxing, or playing Warhammer 40K.
Dr. Glenna Mauldin
PetCure Oncology’s Director of Clinical Research; Designs and oversees prospective and retrospective clinical research studies performed within the PetCure network
Board certified by the American College of Veterinary Internal Medicine in Oncology (1991), and the American College of Veterinary Nutrition (2004)
Has practiced veterinary medical oncology and nutrition for over 30 years in both private practice and academic settings, including The Animal Medical Center in New York City, Louisiana State University in Baton Rouge Louisiana, and VCA Western Veterinary Specialist and Emergency Centre in Calgary, Alberta, Canada.
Currently a sessional instructor in oncology and nutrition at the University of Calgary College of Veterinary Medicine in Calgary, Alberta, Canada
Specialty of Oncology Past President, American College of Veterinary Internal Medicine
Current Vice President, American College of Veterinary Nutrition
Author of over 75 peer reviewed publications, book chapters and scientific abstracts
Lectures frequently at regional, national, and international meetings
Training: Western College of Veterinary Medicine, Saskatoon, Saskatchewan, Canada (DVM); The Animal Medical Center, New York, New York (internship and residency in medical oncology); Cornell University, Ithaca, New York (residency in veterinary nutrition and MS)
Pet parent to four rescued Shetland Sheepdogs (Charlotte, Jenna, Tuscan and Noah) and four horses (Webster, Sarah, Briosa and Genesis RDL)
